correctness.rationale: A tree incidence matrix has trivial edge kernel, so period dividing two is equivalent to exact edgewise sign reversal. The necessary and sufficient signed-gap bounds force independent assignments on a tree, and the rooted coefficient extraction counts each assignment once. Subtree-size monomials encode total chip mass modulo n; the unique constant fixed state is subtracted, and the remaining states split into two-state orbits. The standard-library verifier replays exact recurrence and independent brute edge-gap counts for every labelled tree of orders 1 through 6 (1,442 cases), plus explicit integer dynamics. These finite checks corroborate an infinite proof; they do not substitute for it.

value.rationale: The result gives a uniform polynomial-time exact primitive-orbit census on every labelled finite tree, including each prescribed conserved integer total, for a process with infinite unbounded state space. Unlike a path/star/bistar special-case formula, branching is unrestricted and captured by subtree-size weights. Two nonisomorphic six-vertex degree twins have different primitive-orbit counts (279 and 197) and chip-total residue profiles, furnishing a natural geometry-sensitive dynamical invariant and a reusable graph-dynamics counting method.
